The tumor cells exhibit nuclear atypia, hyperchromasia, and mitotic activity. These microscopic features are characteristic of a leiomyosarcoma.

blind.description: This is a micrograph showing a cellular spindle cell proliferation with mild nuclear atypia and an intersecting fascicular pattern. The tissue demonstrates smooth muscle differentiation with some lymphocytes in the background and no apparent mitoses. The overall histologic features are most consistent with a smooth muscle tumor, such as a leiomyosarcoma.

random.description: This is a micrograph showing a histological section of soft tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The image displays a hypercellular proliferation of spindle-shaped cells arranged in fascicles or a storiform pattern. Nuclear pleomorphism, mitotic figures, and atypical features are visible throughout the field. These histopathological findings are characteristic of a malignant mesenchymal tumor, such as a fibrosarcoma or malignant fibrous histiocytoma.
captions: Acral lentiginous melanoma, in situ pattern. Most cells are arranged in a linear array along the basal layer and a few nests are also present HE

(a) Partial atrophy with atypical features, suspicious for cancer. At low power, several disorganized glands with partially atrophic cytoplasm are present. A few completely atrophic glands are also present. These features are suggestive of partial atrophy (a). At higher magnification, these glands demonstrated bland cytology (b). However, the edge of this lesion appears infiltrative (arrow, a) and it demonstrates immunophenotype identical to cancer (c). Despite the presence of several features of partial atrophy, one cannot rule out cancer.
